welcome: Hello, I'm your coach. Pick a lesson and we'll work through it together. Press Show me at any time and I'll play the shot first.
cue_1: Let's start with cue ball control. This is a straight pot on the blue into the corner. First, the stun shot: strike the cue ball in the centre with a firm, smooth stroke. The cue ball should stop dead where the blue was. Finish it in the gold circle.
cue_2: Now the screw shot. Strike below centre and follow through. The backspin pulls the cue ball back towards you after the pot. Bring it back into the gold circle.
cue_3: And the follow-through, or top. Strike above centre, gently, and the cue ball rolls on after the blue. Stop it in the gold circle, and don't follow it into the pocket.
cue_done: Well done. Stun, screw and top are the three shots you'll use to place the cue ball for your next pot.
cut_1: Cut shots. Imagine a ghost ball touching the red, lined up with the pocket. That's where the cue ball has to be when it makes contact. Aim the centre of the cue ball at the centre of the ghost ball, and pot the red. This one's a half-ball cut.
cut_2: A thinner cut now. The thinner the cut, the less of the red you hit and the more precise you have to be. Trust the ghost ball.
cut_3: And a three-quarter ball pot. Thicker cuts are more forgiving, and the cue ball travels less after contact.
cut_done: Good. With practice you'll see the ghost ball without needing the guide.
dbl_1: The double. The red is close to the cushion, so instead we send it into the cushion and back across the table into the opposite middle pocket. Picture the pocket reflected in the cushion, like a mirror, and pot the red into that reflection. I've drawn the mirror pocket for you. Play it firmly.
dbl_2: Now a double into a corner. Same idea: aim the red at the corner pocket's reflection in the cushion. The cushion takes a little pace off the ball, so it comes off slightly shorter than a perfect mirror. Allow for that.
dbl_done: Excellent. Doubles are never easy, but they win frames when there's nothing else on.
esc_1: You're snookered: the blue is between you and the red. To escape off one cushion, picture the red reflected in the cushion, as far behind it as the red is in front. Aim straight at that reflection, strike the cue ball in the centre, and it will come off the cushion on to the red.
esc_2: Again from a different angle, off the far cushion. Remember, without side the angle off the cushion is close to the angle on.
esc_done: Well escaped. The mirror method gets you out of most snookers.
two_1: A harder one: a two-cushion escape. The pink is guarding the red in the corner. I've worked out a path for you off two cushions. Follow the white line and hit the red first.
two_done: Superb. Two-cushion escapes take practice, so come back to this one.
swv_1: The swerve. When the cushions won't help, bend the cue ball round the obstruction instead. Raise the butt of your cue about twenty to thirty degrees, and strike with side on the side you want the ball to curve towards. Aim a little wide of the blue and let it swerve back on to the red.
swv_done: Lovely. Swerve is one of the hardest shots in the game, so don't worry if it takes a few goes.
brk_1: The break-off. The cue ball is between the brown and the yellow. Clip the end red of the back row thinly, so the cue ball runs off the top and side cushions and back up to baulk, leaving nothing on. Hit a red and bring the cue ball back behind the baulk line.
brk_done: A tidy break-off. That's the course complete. In practice, ask for a coach's tip whenever you're stuck.
tryagain_3: Nearly. Reset and have another look.
